learningObjectives: Identify accessibility issues across visual, auditory, motor, and cognitive experiences.
Apply inclusive interaction and content patterns.
Evaluate interfaces using accessibility-focused design criteria.

activities.title: Accessibility Needs Map
activities.instruction: Explore different accessibility needs and design responses.

content.concept: Inclusive design considers diverse sensory, motor, cognitive, and communication needs throughout the experience.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Accessible Pattern Matcher
activities.instruction: Match each barrier with a suitable design solution.

content.concept: Accessible patterns can include keyboard support, clear labels, sufficient contrast, captions, focus indicators, and understandable feedback.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Keyboard Navigation Lab
activities.instruction: Arrange the correct keyboard focus sequence.

content.concept: Logical focus order allows keyboard users to navigate and operate interface controls predictably.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Accessibility Audit
activities.instruction: Select the accessibility issues in the interface.

content.concept: An accessibility audit checks visual, interaction, content, navigation, and feedback patterns for barriers.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.
